URL: https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy-summary-and-minutes/2026/november-2026
Outlet: Bank of England, published 05 November 2026

Bank of England Monetary Policy Decision – November 2026

Decision: Bank Rate increased to 4% (0.25 percentage point increase)

Vote: 8–1 majority
- 8 members voted for 0.25 percentage point increase
- 1 member (Catherine L Mann) voted for 0.5 percentage point increase

Monetary Policy Summary, November 2026

At its meeting on 4 November 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee voted to raise Bank Rate by a quarter percentage point to 4%. One dissenting member preferred a larger half-percentage-point increase.

Inflation Outlook:
"UK CPI inflation increased to 3.5% in September. It is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year."

The Committee noted that direct energy effects contributed approximately one percentage point to September's inflation reading, though indirect effects on other prices and wages remained limited thus far.

Forward Guidance:
"Monetary policy is not on a pre-set path. The Committee will continue to assess the evidence at each meeting, in particular how likely high energy prices are to feed through to other prices and the economy more broadly, by monitoring the evolution of underlying pay, pricing behaviour, and slack."

Economic Context:
Activity data strengthened unexpectedly, while the Middle East conflict continued driving elevated global energy prices upward from already elevated levels.
